title: Sam Altman says Elon Musk is a ‘bully’ who only respects people who punch him back
source_used: Vanity Fair interview with Sam Altman, Part 1 (https://www.vanityfair.com/story/sam-altman-exclusive-interview-part-1), read in full; Business Insider's write-up of it (the pool item) read for its added context
key_facts: Vanity Fair published a two-part interview with OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman on 5 Oct 2026; the talks were held in San Francisco on 11 Sep and 2 Oct.
Asked about his sparring with Elon Musk on Twitter and the AI industry needing to 'grow up', Altman said 'I don't like bullies, and I think Elon's a bully'.
Altman: 'once in a while you got to punch a bully back in the nose. And I also think Elon, like many bullies, only respects people who do.'
Altman: 'if you want me to be able to work with him, maybe you should be happy I hit back once in a while, but I will work with Elon, of course.'
Altman also said 'I won't call myself a saint' and 'I'm not sure if I'm the one that you're supposed to come after between Elon and me.'

Business Insider adds that Musk has taken to calling Altman 'Scam Altman'; in July Musk wrote 'He takes scamming to a whole new level' and Altman answered by mocking Musk's push for orbital data centres.

Business Insider says the two men's falling-out is at the center of multiple legal battles, and that leaders of OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceXAI, Google and Nvidia signed a White House-driven agreement with some self-imposed safety measures.
Business Insider says Altman told Politico's Decoded podcast there is no single group chat among lab leaders, but they run into each other at conferences and have calls and occasional meetings.
quote_evidence: Look, I don’t like bullies, and I think Elon’s a bully.
And I also think Elon, like many bullies, only respects people who do.
The OpenAI CEO said he would work with Musk, who has taken to calling his one-time ally “Scam Altman,” as the industry grapples with renewed concerns over AI safety.
why_it_matters_hint: The heads of two leading AI rivals trade public insults while their industry tries to agree on safety steps.
event_date: Interview published 5 Oct 2026; held 11 Sep and 2 Oct 2026 (the transcript does not say which session this answer came from)
notes: Pool item is Business Insider's write-up of the Vanity Fair interview; the interview itself (Part 1) was read and the quotes match, so Vanity Fair is credited and linked as the first reporter. The 'Scam Altman' name-calling and the July exchange come from Business Insider only and were not checked elsewhere. Same interview as C05-04.
